newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Rebels roll out big guns in southern Albania town.
newsitem.headline: Rebels roll out big guns in southern Albania town.

text.p: Anti-government groups, many of them youths, took firm control of the southern Albanian town of Tepelene on Thursday, rolling big guns into the central square, a Reuter reporter said.

Men and youths had taken guns seized from an army barracks and hundreds were parading through the town firing into the air. Women and children were stripping clean virtually all other items from the building, mainly clothing and blankets, he said.
Former army officers said they would remain in place until the resignation of President Sali Berisha, re-elected to a five-year term by parliament this week.
"We will not return our weapons until Berisha resigns," said one colonel. "The army in southern Albania has gone over to the side of the people."

Shops in the city were empty and residents said supplies had been halted by army roadblocks in Gjirokaster to the south. "We have food shortages. I haven't seen bread for the past two days," said one elderly woman, Melpo Karali.

Albania's army is meeting determined resistance as it pushes through volatile southern regions under state of emergency regulations passed by parliament last weekend. More than 20 people have been killed in the latest wave of violence which erupted last weekend in the port of Vlore.
